s0601.literal: duan or is written duan; "shou" is an error for the character duan."
s0601.idiomatic: Duan may also be written duan; shou is a miswriting of duan."

s0602.literal: Changed to Cloud Dragon Spirit-Beast Gate—"Spirit-Beast Gate" is "Spirit-Tiger Gate," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0602.idiomatic: Emended to Cloud Dragon Spirit-Beast Gate: Spirit-Beast Gate is Spirit-Tiger Gate, changed for Tang taboo.

s0603.literal: Trustworthy Might General, Inspector of Jiangzhou, Prince of Changsha Shujian made Cloud Battle-ax General and Central Army Inspector—note: in Taijian year 4 he was made Eastern Central Commander, Administrator of Wu commandery, Prince of Changsha Shujian, made Firm Resolution General and Inspector of Jiangzhou, matching his main biography; afterward no advance or change of military title is recorded; here "Trustworthy Might General" is suspected to be in error.
s0603.idiomatic: On "Prince of Changsha Shujian, trustworthy might general and inspector of Jiangzhou, made cloud battle-ax general and central army inspector": in Taijian year 4 he was made firm resolution general and inspector of Jiangzhou, as in his biography, with no later change of rank recorded; trustworthy might general here is probably wrong.

s0604.literal: Moreover on bingchen of the twelfth month of this year, the newly appointed Cloud Battle-ax General and Inspector of Yingzhou, Prince of Changsha Shujian, was made Pacify-the-Yue Central Commander and Inspector of Guangzhou; his main biography also says that in Taijian year 7 he was advanced to Cloud Battle-ax General and Inspector of Yingzhou.
s0604.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on bingchen of this year the newly appointed cloud battle-ax general and Yingzhou inspector, Prince of Changsha Shujian, was made pacify-the-Yue central commander and Guangzhou inspector; his biography likewise has him advanced to cloud battle-ax general and Yingzhou inspector in Taijian year 7.

s0605.literal: The "Central Army Inspector" here is suspected to be corrupt.
s0605.idiomatic: Central army inspector here is probably erroneous.

s0606.literal: [Fifth month] gengyin—supplied according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan of Chen in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0606.idiomatic: [Fifth month] gengyin—restored per the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

s0607.literal: Note: that year the fourth month began on jiyou; there was no gengyin;
s0607.idiomatic: Note: that year the fourth month began on jiyou; gengyin does not occur.

s0608.literal: The fifth month began on wuyin; the thirteenth day was gengyin.
s0608.idiomatic: The fifth month began on wuyin; the thirteenth day was gengyin.

s0609.literal: Prince of Changsha Shujian, General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou, made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou—note: Shujian in the sixth month of that year was Inspector of Hezhou and advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
s0609.idiomatic: On making Prince of Changsha Shujian, general who pacifies the south and Xiangzhou inspector, general who pacifies the west and Yingzhou inspector: in the sixth month of that year he was Hezhou inspector and was advanced to general who pacifies the north.

s0610.literal: His main biography also says that before he was General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou he had been General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hezhou.
s0610.idiomatic: His biography also says that before he was general who pacifies the west and Yingzhou inspector he had been general who pacifies the north and Hezhou inspector.

s0611.literal: Here "General Who Pacifies the South" and "Inspector of Xiangzhou" should be errors for "General Who Pacifies the North" and "Inspector of Hezhou."
s0611.idiomatic: General who pacifies the south and Xiangzhou inspector here should read general who pacifies the north and Hezhou inspector.

s0612.literal: At that time the Inspector of Xiangzhou was Prince of Shixing Shuling.
s0612.idiomatic: At that time Xiangzhou inspector was Prince of Shixing Shuling.

s0615.literal: [zi]—changed according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan of Chen in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0615.idiomatic: [zi]—emended per the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

s0616.literal: Note: that year the second month began on jiachen; there was no renwu.
s0616.idiomatic: Note: that year the second month began on jiachen; renwu does not occur.

s0617.literal: Arrears of rent-field grain, rice, millet, summer levy silk, gauze, raw silk, cloth, wheat, etc., for years six and seven—"wheat" in Essentials of Governance 489 reads "cloth."
s0617.idiomatic: On "arrears of field rent, grain, rice, millet, summer levy silk, gauze, raw silk, cloth, and wheat for years six and seven": Essentials of Governance 489 reads cloth for wheat.

s0619.literal: Left Supporting General—note: his main biography says Ling in Taijian year 8 was made Right Supporting General, with no further change afterward; this differs.
s0619.idiomatic: On "left supporting general": his biography has Xu Ling made right supporting general in Taijian year 8 with no later change; this passage differs.

s0620.literal: [Summer] fifth month yisi—note: above reads "third month dingwei"; by precedent this should read "summer, fifth month"; clearly the character summer is missing; all editions alike omit it; now supplied.
s0620.idiomatic: [Summer] fifth month yisi—above reads third month dingwei; by precedent this should be summer, fifth month; summer has clearly dropped out and all editions omit it; now restored.

s0621.literal: Yao's "I charge you, Houji and Qi, Zhu Wu"—"Zhu Wu" is "Zhu Hu," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0621.idiomatic: On Yao's charge to Houji and Qi, Zhu Wu: Zhu Wu is Zhu Hu, changed for Tang taboo.

s0622.literal: And Xu, Shanyang, Yangping, Matou, Qin, Liyang, Pei, North Qiao, South Liang, and the other nine
s0622.idiomatic: And Xu, Shanyang, Yangping, Matou, Qin, Liyang, Pei, North Qiao, South Liang, and the other nine

s0624.literal: [jun]—Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories says zhou should be jun.
s0624.idiomatic: [jun]—Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories says zhou should be commanderies.

s0625.literal: Note: the places listed above are all commandery names; now emended accordingly.
s0625.idiomatic: The places named above are all commanderies; emended accordingly.

s0627.literal: [huan]—changed according to Hu Zhu on the Comprehensive Mirror and Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories.
s0627.idiomatic: [huan]—emended per Hu Zhu on the Comprehensive Mirror and Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories.

s0628.literal: Note: Qian Daxin says xuan should be huan; Huanzhou is Sui's Jiyang commandery.
s0628.idiomatic: Note: Qian Daxin holds xuan should be huan; Huanzhou is Sui's Jiyang commandery.

s0629.literal: Lu Mountain, Zeng Mountain, Dunyang, Yingcheng, Pingjing, Wuyang, Shangming, Yun River, and the other eight garrisons submitted—"Yun River" was originally corrupt as Juan River; all editions alike are corrupt.
s0629.idiomatic: On "Lu Mountain, Zeng Mountain, Dunyang, Yingcheng, Pingjing, Wuyang, Shangming, Yun River, and seven other garrisons submitted": Yun River was miswritten Juan River in all editions.

s0630.literal: Note: Lu Mountain and the other eight garrisons are all within present Hubei province.
s0630.idiomatic: Lu Mountain and the other eight garrisons all lie in present-day Hubei.

s0631.literal: Geography of the Sui: "Angui—in the Western Wei they set up Yun River commandery; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished.
s0631.idiomatic: Sui Geography: "Angui—in Western Wei they established Yun River commandery; at the start of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished.

s0632.literal: " Angui's old seat is northwest of present Suixian in Hubei.
s0632.idiomatic: " Angui's former seat is northwest of present Suixian in Hubei.

s0633.literal: Yun River garrison should be that place.
s0633.idiomatic: Yun River garrison should be at that site.

s0634.literal: "Juan River" in Essentials of Governance 215 correctly reads "Yun River"; now corrected.
s0634.idiomatic: Essentials of Governance 215 correctly reads Yun River for Juan River; emended.

s0635.literal: Zhou Prince of Guangling Yi, Cao Yao, leading his forces to submit—Hall edition textual note says the History of the Southern Dynasties has the character army before lord.
s0635.idiomatic: On "Zhou Prince of Guangling Yi, Cao Yao, leading his forces to submit": the Hall edition notes that the Southern History has army before lord.

s0638.literal: [shi] lost support—changed according to all editions.
s0638.idiomatic: [shi] lost their livelihood—emended per all editions.

s0639.literal: Danyang, Wuxing, Jinling, Jianxing, Yixing, Donghai, Xinyi, Chenliu, Jiangling, and the other ten commanderies—Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories says: "Counting them now, there are only nine commanderies."
s0639.idiomatic: On "Danyang, Wuxing, Jinling, Jianxing, Yixing, Donghai, Xinyi, Chenliu, Jiangling, and the other ten commanderies": Qian Daxin's Examination counts only nine commanderies.

s0642.literal: [zhu] offices and annual field-tax salaries—changed according to Essentials of Governance 489.
s0642.idiomatic: [zhu] offices and annual field-tax stipends—emended per Essentials of Governance 489.

s0643.literal: [An] Right General, Dan-yang Intendant Xu Ling made Central Secretariat Supervisor and concurrent Crown Prince Grand Tutor—note: Ling's main biography says that in Taijian year 10 he again became Protector General and soon moved to Secure-the-Right General and Dan-yang Intendant.
s0643.idiomatic: On "[An] right general, Dan-yang intendant Xu Ling made central secretariat supervisor and concurrent crown prince grand tutor": his biography has him made protector general again in Taijian year 10, then soon secure-the-right general and Dan-yang intendant.

s0644.literal: The character An is missing here; now supplied.
s0644.idiomatic: An has dropped out here; now restored.
